title: Introduce presubmit slim profiles and release safety oracle
author: Aisha Patil
release_notes: Adds lightweight presubmit profiles to speed CI for small changes; introduces a small release-safety oracle that validates dependency provenance and release-window constraints before promotion; no public API changes.
description: Motivation: Our presubmit lanes run expensive linters and full integration matrices even for trivial doc/README or single-package tweaks. This PR introduces 'slim' presubmit profiles that are diff-aware and run a minimal fast-path pipeline for small, low-risk changes. It also introduces a tiny 'release-safety-oracle' used by release automation to validate dependency provenance and enforce a configurable release window before promoting release candidates. Goals: reduce average presubmit latency for common edits, reduce CI cost, and add a safety gate for automated promotions.

review_comments: Marco Nguyen: Nicely scoped. Two requests: make the router classification deterministic (use first matching rule) and add a metric for 'skipped-heavy-lint' so we can measure impact.
Aisha Patil (author): Addressed both: router now uses ordered rules with stable tie-break, added prometheus metric ci_presubmit_skipped_lint_total and updated tests.
Sofia Blake: Release oracle looks good. Please add a short-circuit to allow emergency manual override via infra flag and log detailed provenance checks to the audit log.
Aisha Patil: Added override flag infra/flags/ci.json and audit logging; included example in docs.
testing_summary: Unit tests: 32 new tests, router coverage 88%. Local bench: median presubmit runtime for small diffs reduced from 4m20s to 1m10s (CI synthetic). Integration: release pipeline exercised with canary enabled; oracle prevented a simulated promotion when dependency origin was unverified. CI checks initially had one flaky e2e caused by a runner image pull; rerun fixed it. All checks green on final run.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: misclassification causing skipped required checks. Mitigation: staged rollout via infra/flags (10% -> 50% -> 100%), explicit opt-out label (ci/no-slim) for PRs, full-coverage fallback that re-routes if tests detect modified stack-level files. Rollback: restore scripts/ci/legacy-router.sh and flip feature flag to off. Monitoring: added ci.presubmit.skipped_lint, ci.router.classifications and release.oracle.rejections metrics.
rollout_plan: 1) Enable slim profiles in canary (10%) for 48h; 2) monitor latency and skipped_lint metrics; 3) increase to 50% for 72h; 4) full rollout and announce to engineering channels. Release-safety-oracle enabled for nightly promotions first, then for on-demand promotions after a week.
